title: Krull-Akizuki Noetherianity for intermediate rings
statement: Let R be a Noetherian domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] of Krull dimension 1 [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] with fraction field K, let L/K be a finite field extension [def-pc-field-extension], and let D be a ring with R ⊆ D ⊆ L. Then D is Noetherian.

proof.text: Let I be a nonzero ideal of D and choose 0 != a in I. Since L/K is finite, a satisfies a nonzero polynomial over K; clearing denominators gives an equation c_m a^m + ... + c_0 = 0 with c_i in R and c_0 != 0. Taking a polynomial of least degree, c_0 is nonzero, while c_m a^m + ... + c_1 a belongs to I, so c_0 belongs to I cap R. Thus every nonzero ideal I of D contains a nonzero element x of R. (The zero ideal is already finitely generated.)

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 10.119.12 (Tag 00PG), proof: Lemma 10.30.8 gives a nonzero element of I intersect R; equivalently the minimal-polynomial argument

proof.text: Fix a nonzero x in I cap R. Choose a K-basis of the finite extension L/K, identifying L with K^{oplus r} for r = [L : K]. Then D is an R-submodule of K^{oplus r}, so [lem-sc-finite-length-global-submodule] gives finite length for D/xD as an R-module. The submodule I/xD therefore has finite length, hence is generated by finitely many elements as an R-module. Lifting those generators to I and adjoining x generates I as a D-ideal, because xD is generated by x and R is contained in D. Thus every ideal of D is finitely generated, so D is Noetherian.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 10.119.12 (Tag 00PG), proof: I/xA is a submodule of A/xA; Lemma 10.119.11 gives finite length of A/xA; hence I is finitely generated
